statement: Let M = 10^9+7. Call a non-empty finite ordered binary tree valid for arr if: every node label is an element of arr; every leaf has no children; every internal node has exactly two children, and if its label is w and the root labels of its left and right children are a and b respectively, then w = a*b. Let N(arr) be the total number of valid trees for arr. Whenever num_factored_binary_trees(arr) returns a result r, r = N(arr) mod M.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 2 <= arr[i] <= 10^9; all entries of arr are distinct (for every i,j, if 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= j < len(arr), and arr[i] = arr[j], then i = j).

statement: For every arr satisfying the preconditions, num_factored_binary_trees(arr) returns a result r; it does not fail (no panic, out-of-bounds access, or arithmetic overflow).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 2 <= arr[i] <= 10^9; all entries of arr are distinct (for every i,j, if 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= j < len(arr), and arr[i] = arr[j], then i = j).

statement: Whenever num_factored_binary_trees(arr) returns a result r, 0 <= r <= 10^9+6.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 2 <= arr[i] <= 10^9; all entries of arr are distinct (for every i,j, if 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= j < len(arr), and arr[i] = arr[j], then i = j).

statement: Let a tree be valid for arr if it is a non-empty finite ordered binary tree with labels in arr, leaves childless, and every internal node with label w and child root labels a,b satisfies w = a*b. For v in arr, let T(v) be the number of valid trees for arr rooted at v. Let N(arr) be the total number of valid trees for arr. Then N(arr) = sum over v in arr of T(v). Consequently, whenever num_factored_binary_trees(arr) returns r, r = (sum over v in arr of T(v)) mod (10^9+7).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 2 <= arr[i] <= 10^9; all entries of arr are distinct (for every i,j, if 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= j < len(arr), and arr[i] = arr[j], then i = j).

statement: If num_factored_binary_trees(arr) returns r and num_factored_binary_trees(arr') returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: arr and arr' each satisfy: 1 <= len <= 1000; all entries in [2,10^9]; all entries distinct. Also, for every integer x, x is an element of arr if and only if x is an element of arr'.

statement: Whenever num_factored_binary_trees(arr) returns r, r = len(arr) mod (10^9+7). Since len(arr) <= 1000 < 10^9+7, this means r = len(arr).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 2 <= arr[i] <= 10^9; all entries of arr are distinct; len(arr) >= 2; and for every a,b,v in arr, a*b != v.
1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 2 <= arr[i] <= 10^9; all entries of arr are distinct; len(arr) = 1.
